doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Television, vocal albums and orchestral craft
title: Using Joe Maini and Art Pepper
summary: Mandel says he used Joe Maini on everything once he found him, and used Art Pepper on the Hoagy Carmichael album after playing with him in Latin bands in the late 1940s.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: So what else did you use Joe on besides, Ring-a-Ding-Ding!
Everything, once I discovered him, I wouldn’t let him out of my sight.
He was kind of for you what Art Pepper was for Marty Paich.
I guess so, but I loved Art Pepper too but Art Pepper wasn’t around a lot of the time.

Art Pepper was a marvelous player, I used him on the Hoagy Carmichael album. I used to play with him in the Spanish bands, you know when I was playing in the Latin bands. We called them Spanish bands, they weren’t Spanish, they were Puerto Rican or Cuban, that was in the late 40s.
How well did you get to know him?
Would you like to talk about him a bit.
